newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn allots 8.59 bln dmk T-notes at 99.80 and over.
newsitem.headline: Bonn allots 8.59 bln dmk T-notes at 99.80 and over.

text.p: The German government on Tuesday allocated 8.585 billion marks of two-year, 3.75 percent Treasury notes at a lowest accepted price of 99.80, the Bundesbank as issuing agent said.
The average yield at issue was 3.83 percent and the weighted average price was 99.84, the Bundesbank said.
The Bundesbank said it was retaining 3.415 billion marks of the issue for market-smoothing purposes, bringing the total volume of the issue to 12 billion marks.

Bids for the issue totalled 13.698 billion marks and the weighted average price of all bids was 99.72, the Bundesbank said. Bids at the lowest accepted rates and bids which did not cite a price were allocated in full.
The notes mature on March 19, 1999. The first interest payment is on March 19, 1998. The settlement date is on March 20 and the notes will be listed on securities exchanges on March 21.
